root_cause.text: The iomap read path incorrectly relied solely on checking if all bytes of a folio were submitted to hand off folio ownership to the IO helper, failing to account for cases where I/O granularity is smaller than the folio size (even though the block size matches the folio size), which allows partial I/O completions that can cause iomap_read_end() to be called on a folio already owned by the IO helper, leading to invalid folio access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition in `iomap_read_folio_iter()` from `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len)` to `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len || !ifs)` and the commit message explicitly states: "It did not handle the case where 1 << inode->i_blkbits matches the folio size but is different from the granularity used for the IO... the condition ... will not invalidate ctx->cur_folio, and iomap_read_end() will still be called on the folio even though the IO helper owns it."

intent_record.intent_summary: Declare a local variable `ifs` of type `struct iomap_folio_state *` for future use within `iomap_read_folio_iter`.
intent_record.what: Added a local variable declaration `struct iomap_folio_state *ifs;` inside the function `iomap_read_folio_iter`.
intent_record.how: Introduces a new pointer variable `ifs` that is not yet used; no immediate runtime behavior change.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing assignment of ifs_alloc return value in iomap_read_folio_iter, which caused later use of uninitialized pointer.
intent_record.what: Changed a call to ifs_alloc from a void expression to an assignment to variable ifs, capturing the return value.
intent_record.how: The return value of ifs_alloc is now stored in ifs, which is used later in the function, correcting a bug where the pointer was uninitialized or stale.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix folio ownership handoff in iomap_read_folio_iter for folios without iomap_folio_state when block size matches folio size but I/O granularity is smaller.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition for setting ctx->cur_folio to NULL from only when bytes_submitted equals folio_len to also when ifs (iomap_folio_state) is NULL. Updated the comment to explain the new condition.
intent_record.how: The change ensures that a folio is handed off to the IO helper (cur_folio = NULL) not only when all its bytes have been submitted for I/O, but also when there is no iomap_folio_state attached to it. This prevents the folio from being incorrectly retained when the block size matches folio size but the filesystem/block device uses a smaller I/O granularity, which can lead to missed completions or other errors.

The group's intent directly matches the vulnerability description: fixing folio ownership handoff in iomap_read_folio_iter for the case where block size matches folio size but I/O granularity is smaller, which is the exact scenario leading to the invalid folio access.

candidates.rationale: This condition incorrectly assumes that ownership of the folio can be handed off to the IO helper only when all bytes have been submitted. It fails to account for cases where I/O granularity is smaller than the folio size, allowing partial I/O completions that cause invalid access.
This statement hands off folio ownership based on the flawed condition, leading to potential double completion or use-after-free when partial I/Os complete.
